title: Delegated-Approval-Workflows-and-Audit-Telemetry-Spec
content:
Summary:
This design doc defines a delegated approval (delegation) model layered on top of RBAC v2, and specifies the audit telemetry (event schema) and SIEM export mapping needed to evidence delegated grants for compliance reviews. The goal is to allow temporary, auditable, and revocable delegation flows for operators and product teams while ensuring all proof-of-action is exportable to enterprise SIEMs (Elastic, Splunk, Chronicle).

Motivation and problems addressed:
- Current RBAC v1 lacks a first-class, time-limited delegation primitive; teams currently share long-lived service accounts or escalate via ad-hoc Slack approvals (poor audit trail).
- Compliance requests (SOX/ISO/PCI) demand per-action evidence tying permission grants to approvers, TTLs, and automated revocation records.
- Existing audit logs are tokenized and missing structured fields that SIEMs require for alerting and retention policies.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Delegation primitives: request, approve, escalate, consume, revoke, and auto-revoke TTLs.
- End-to-end telemetry: event types, required attributes, severity levels, and consumer IDs.
- SIEM export mapping: recommended ECS-aligned fields and examples for Elastic and Splunk.
- Rollout plan: phased migration steps, toggles, and verification checks.

Non-goals:
- Changing core RBAC policy syntax (this sits on top of existing RBAC v2 policies).
- Replacing existing SIEM ingestion pipelines (we provide mapping and a connector).

Design overview (high level):
1) Delegation model:
   - Actors: requester, approver(s), delegate (principal receiving rights), and operator (system process).
   - Grant types: "action-bound" (one-time action), "session-bound" (time-limited session with scope), and "role-temporary" (temporary role assignment).
   - Approval modes: single-approver, multi-approver (threshold), and auto-approve policy (for low-risk scopes).
   - Guardrails: TTL default 1h (configurable per org), max TTL 24h, explicit revocation API, and automatic revocation on policy change.

2) UX/workflow notes (quick):
   - In-console flow: requester fills scope (resource + action), reason, and desired TTL. Approver gets Slack/console notification. Approver clicks approve -> system records approval artifact and issues time-limited token or role binding.
   - CLI flow: rbac delegate request -> returns request id; approve via rbac approve --id or via console link.

3) Enforcement surface:
   - Implemented as an admission layer in the authorization shim. Delegation grants are realized as ephemeral role-bindings stored in the policy datastore with explicit start/end timestamps and a unique grant id.
   - Serving runtime checks both active RBAC policies and ephemeral grants (fast path: cache grant ids with TTL).

Audit telemetry (required fields):
All events MUST include the following canonical attributes. These are required for downstream SIEM correlation and audit evidence packages.
- event_id: GUID
- event_time: ISO8601 UTC
- event_type: one of [delegation.requested, delegation.approved, delegation.denied, delegation.issued, delegation.revoked, delegation.expired]
- grant_id: GUID (links all events for a single delegation lifecycle)
- request_id: GUID (if a request triggered the grant)
- principal: subject receiving the rights (user/service principal id)
- actor: user id who performed the action (requester or approver)
- resource: canonical resource id (resource-type:resource-id)
- action: verb being delegated (e.g., data:read, model:deploy)
- scope: JSON-stringified scope summary (bounded to 1024 chars)
- ttl_seconds: integer (original TTL)
- issued_token_id: id of ephemeral token (if applicable)
- reason: free text reason supplied by requester (optional for automated approvals but captured)
- outcome: success|failure|denied
- source_ip: requester IP (if relevant)
- org_id: customer or org context
- service: logical service name (e.g., rbac-service, console)

Note: event_type must exactly match values above for simple filtering in SIEM.

Example event (delegation.approved):
{
  "event_id": "d3f9a8c2-7f1a-4a6c-9b6f-ef4f2a1b6c08",
  "event_time": "2025-02-01T15:02:33Z",
  "event_type": "delegation.approved",
  "grant_id": "g-0a1b2c3d",
  "request_id": "r-4e5f6g7h",
  "principal": "svc-ml-trainer@redwood",
  "actor": "alice@redwood.com",
  "resource": "project:atlas/model:deploy",
  "action": "model:deploy",
  "scope": "{\"regions\":[\"us-west1\"]}",
  "ttl_seconds": "3600",
  "issued_token_id": "tkn-99ab",
  "reason": "hotfix rollout",
  "outcome": "success",
  "source_ip": "34.76.12.9",
  "org_id": "org-123",
  "service": "rbac-delegation-service"
}

Severity and retention hints:
- delegation.requested / delegation.approved / delegation.denied: severity=info
- delegation.revoked (manual) / delegation.expired (auto): severity=warning
- suspicious patterns (multi-approver bypass, repeated quick TTL requests): severity=critical (upstream rule, not a separate event type)

SIEM export mapping recommendations:
- Target canonical mapping: Elastic Common Schema (ECS) fields where possible. Minimal mapping:
  - ecs.event.id <= event_id
  - ecs.event.created <= event_time
  - ecs.event.action <= event_type
  - user.name <= actor
  - user.id <= principal
  - url.path/query or service.name <= service
  - process.command_line <= action + resource (if needed)
  - network.direction / source.ip <= source_ip
  - labels.org_id <= org_id
  - labels.grant_id/request_id <= grant_id/request_id

- For Splunk (HEC) use the same canonical event as JSON payload and set _sourcetype=rbac:delegation; ensure timestamp field maps to event_time.

Export pipeline options (tradeoffs):
1) Push-based Kinesis/Kafka -> log-shipper -> SIEM (low-latency, requires retention SLOs)
2) Batch export from audit-store to S3 -> SIEM ingest (lower cost, higher latency; good for quarterly evidence packages)
3) Dual-write: real-time push for high severity events + batch for bulk evidence (recommended default)

Privacy and PII considerations:
- reason and principal fields may contain user-identifiable info. Apply redaction policy configurable by org (full, partial, none) before pushing to third-party SIEMs.

Evidence automation and compliance package generation:
- Evidence package for an audit window (time range + org): query grant_id set, pull all related events, policy snapshots (policy blob at grant time), approver user records, issued_token metadata, and revocation proof.
- Provide an API /audit-packages?org_id=...&from=...&to=... that returns a signed tarball with manifest.json and a signature using org KMS.

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 - Lab (Q1): implement delegation primitives in a feature branch; unit tests and local telemetry; no exports enabled.
Phase 1 - Canary (Q2): enable for 3 internal teams (SRE, Applied ML, Console). Dual-write telemetry to internal ES cluster. Run SOC tabletop exercises and verify evidence package flow.
Phase 2 - Org opt-in (Q3): enable for customer orgs via org setting; provide docs for PII redaction and SIEM connector configuration.
Phase 3 - Org-mandatory / Migration window (Q4): for new RBAC v2 rollouts require delegation telemetry on by default and deprecate long-lived ad-hoc service grants. Provide 60-day migration drift window and automated remediation scripts.

Migration checklist (operational):
- Add feature flag: delegation-enabled per-org
- Instrument metrics: grants_created, grants_revoked, grants_expired, approval_latency_ms, approvals_by_policy
- SIEM connector config wizard in Console
- Audit package endpoint and signed export service
- Run migration dry-run: generate evidence packages for 30 days and validate against compliance checklists

KPIs and verification criteria:
- 100% of delegation.approved events include a valid grant_id and actor for canary orgs
- Approval latency median < 30s for single-approver flows (for internal teams)
- Evidence package completeness: >= 99% of grants in window have full event chain (requested -> approved -> issued/expired/revoked)

UX notes for Console + CLI:
- Console: clear visibility into active grants, TTL countdown, and quick revoke button. Link to evidence package for a grant.
- CLI: rbac grants list --org=org-123 includes grant_id, principal, actor, expires_at, and reason. CLI can call rbac audit-packages --grant g-... to fetch signed evidence.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Backfill strategy for existing long-lived service accounts: convert into grants with retroactive issuance events? (proposal: create synthetic requested/approved events and mark as migrated)
- How to model nested delegations (A delegates to B, B delegates to C) and whether to allow transitive delegation beyond 1 hop. Proposed default: disallow transitive delegation without explicit policy.

Next steps:
- Engineering: spike for ephemeral token lifecycle and grant cache (owner: Marcus Liu, JIRA: JIRA-SC-988)
- Security: finalize PII redaction defaults and retention policy (owner: Claire O'Neill)
- Product: finalize console flows and notify affected teams (owner: Diego Ramos)

Appendix: quick references
- Approval API endpoints: POST /v1/delegation/requests, POST /v1/delegation/requests/{id}/approve, POST /v1/delegation/requests/{id}/revoke
- Evidence API: GET /v1/audit-packages?org_id={org}&from={iso}&to={iso}
- Related tickets: JIRA-SC-987, JIRA-SC-988, github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-prs/pull/412
